why: Carbon dioxide enters leaves and is used to make food.

question: Which gas is released by plants during photosynthesis?
why: Oxygen is a by-product of making food.

question: The green pigment that traps sunlight in leaves is
why: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

question: The tiny openings on the surface of leaves are called
why: Gases and water vapour pass through stomata.

question: Xylem vessels carry
d: water and minerals from roots to leaves
why: Xylem carries water and minerals upward.

question: Phloem carries
c: food made in the leaves to other parts
why: Phloem moves prepared food to all parts of the plant.

question: A leaf kept in sunlight is boiled in alcohol and tested with iodine. A blue-black colour shows
why: Iodine turns blue-black with starch, a product of photosynthesis.

question: A potted plant is kept in complete darkness for 36 hours and a leaf is tested with iodine. The leaf
why: In darkness there is no photosynthesis, so no starch is stored.

question: Which part of a plant absorbs water and minerals from the soil?
why: Roots take water and minerals from the soil.

question: Which statement about plant respiration is correct?
c: Plants take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide, day and night
d: Plants take in carbon dioxide only
why: All living cells respire all the time.

question: A variegated leaf has green and white patches. After sunlight and an iodine test, which patches turn blue-black?
why: Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis, so only green patches make starch.

question: Water rises from roots to the leaves of a tall tree mainly because
c: water evaporating from leaves pulls more water up through xylem
why: Loss of water from leaves pulls water up.

question: Which pair correctly gives the inputs of photosynthesis?
d: Carbon dioxide and water, with sunlight
why: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and light to make food.

question: A polythene bag is tied over a leafy branch in sunshine. Droplets collect inside after a few hours because
a: the leaves lose water vapour through stomata
why: Water vapour from leaves condenses on the cool bag.

question: In bright sunlight, a plant's net gas exchange shows more oxygen released than used. Why?
b: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
why: Photosynthesis happens only in light, while respiration is continuous.

question: A water plant in a jar gives off many bubbles in sunlight but few in shade. The bubbles are mostly
why: More light means more photosynthesis, so more oxygen.

question: A ring of bark is removed from a stem. Over days, the stem swells just above the ring because
d: food from leaves piles up where phloem is cut
why: The phloem carrying food downward is blocked.

question: An object that gives out its own light is called
why: Luminous objects such as the Sun make their own light.

question: We see the Moon because it
why: The Moon does not make light; it reflects sunlight.

question: Light travels in
why: Light travels in straight lines, which is why shadows have sharp edges.

question: Which material is opaque?
why: Wood blocks light; clear glass, air and clean water let it pass.

question: Frosted glass lets some light through but we cannot see clearly. It is
why: Frosted glass lets light through but scatters it, so it is translucent.

question: In a plane mirror, the left-right swap in the image is called
why: A plane mirror swaps left and right, which is called lateral inversion.

question: Which three things are needed to form a shadow?
d: Source of light, opaque object and screen
why: A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

question: The word AMBULANCE is written reversed on its front so that
a: it reads correctly in a driver's mirror
why: The reversed word looks correct in the rear-view mirror of the driver ahead because of lateral inversion.

question: The image formed by a pinhole camera is
why: Rays from the top of an object pass the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, giving an inverted image.

question: A periscope uses
c: two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees
why: Two mirrors at 45 degrees turn light twice, letting you see over obstacles.

question: A torch is moved closer to a book on a table in a dark room. The book's shadow on the wall
why: A source nearer the object blocks more light angles, so a bigger shadow forms.

question: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror at 40 degrees to the normal. The reflected ray makes with the normal an angle of
why: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 40 degrees.

question: We cannot see the shadow of a bird flying very high because
d: the shadow falls far away and becomes faint and spread out
why: The shadow falls very far from the bird, so it is faint and spread out.

question: The pinhole of a pinhole camera is made larger. The image becomes
why: A bigger hole lets more light in, but rays spread, so the image is brighter yet blurred.

question: Between a lamp and a wall, a student places cardboard, wax paper and clear glass one at a time. The shadows are
why: Opaque cardboard gives a dark shadow, wax paper a faint one, and clear glass almost none.

question: Sunlight through tree leaves makes round bright patches on the ground because
c: small gaps work like pinholes forming round images of the Sun
why: Each small gap acts as a pinhole and makes a round image of the Sun.

question: In a periscope, the two mirrors are placed
d: parallel to each other, each at 45 degrees to the tube
why: Mirrors parallel at 45 degrees turn the light twice so you see over a wall.

question: A boy's shadow is longer at 4 pm than at noon because
a: the Sun is lower in the sky
why: When the Sun is lower in the sky, shadows are longer.

question: Day and night happen because the Earth
b: moves around the Sun in a day
d: moves closer to and away from the Sun
why: As Earth spins, the half facing the Sun has day while the other half has night.

question: The Earth completes one rotation in about
why: Earth takes about 24 hours for one rotation, which makes one day and night.

question: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in about
why: The Earth takes about 365 days.

question: The path of the Earth around the Sun is called its
why: Earth's fixed path around the Sun is called its orbit.

question: A solar eclipse happens when the
a: Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
b: Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
c: Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
why: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks sunlight.

question: A lunar eclipse happens when the
a: Moon is between the Sun and the Earth
b: Earth is between the Sun and the Moon
c: Sun is between the Earth and the Moon
d: Moon is farthest from the Earth
why: Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when Earth lies between the Sun and Moon.

question: Seasons change mainly because
a: Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun
b: Earth moves nearer to the Sun in summer
c: the Sun moves up and down
why: The tilt changes how much sunlight each hemisphere gets during the year.

question: The Sun seems to rise in the east because
a: the Sun really moves around the Earth
b: Earth rotates from west to east
c: the Earth goes around the Sun in a day
why: Earth spins from west to east, so the Sun only appears to move from east to west.

question: A leap year has an extra day because
a: Earth spins slower every fourth year
c: Earth takes about 365 1/4 days to go around the Sun
why: The extra quarter days add up to one day every four years, added as 29 February.

question: It is safe to watch a lunar eclipse with the eyes but not a solar eclipse because
a: the Moon is too hot to look at
b: a lunar eclipse is much brighter
c: a lunar eclipse happens only in the day
d: the Sun's light can damage the eyes even when it is partly hidden
why: Looking at the Sun can damage the eyes, while the eclipsed Moon is not harmful to view.

question: The stars seem to move across the night sky because
b: stars revolve around Earth every night
why: Earth's spin makes stars appear to drift across the sky.

question: Different stars are seen in different months because
a: stars move to new places each month
d: the Sun moves across the stars
why: As Earth goes around the Sun, the night side faces different stars in different months.

question: If Earth's axis were not tilted, then
b: there would be no day and night
c: it would be summer everywhere all year
d: winter would last longer in India
why: Without the tilt, sunlight would fall the same way all year, so there would be no seasons.

question: A total solar eclipse is seen only from a narrow strip of Earth because
a: the Moon is larger than Earth
b: the Moon's dark shadow on Earth is small
c: eclipses happen only at the poles
why: The Moon's darkest shadow is a small spot on Earth, so only a narrow strip sees totality.

question: The smaller Moon can fully cover the Sun because
a: the Moon is larger than the Sun
b: the Sun is dimmer than the Moon
c: the Moon is much closer to Earth than the Sun is
d: the Moon is made of a dark material
why: The Moon is much closer to us than the Sun, so it appears about the same size and can cover it.

question: When it is summer in India (northern hemisphere) the southern hemisphere
a: also has summer, getting the same light
d: has winter because it is tilted away from the Sun
why: When the northern hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, the southern hemisphere tilts away and has winter.

question: Which pairing is right?
a: Solar eclipse on new moon day; lunar eclipse on full moon day
b: Solar on full moon; lunar on new moon
why: A solar eclipse needs the Moon between Sun and Earth (new moon); a lunar eclipse needs Earth between (full moon).

question: In June, days in the northern hemisphere are longer because
a: Earth is nearer to the Sun in June
b: the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
c: the Sun moves around the Earth
d: the Moon pulls sunlight to India
why: The northern hemisphere tilted towards the Sun gets more hours of daylight.
